chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and he was a pilgrim with us, said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) via the hand of my father; may I be sacrificed for you.
Indeed, our companions differed regarding the Sa'a; some of them say the Fitra is by the Medinite Sa'a, and some of them say by the Iraqi Sa'a.
So he wrote to me: The Sa'a is six Ratls by the Medinite measure, and nine Ratls by the Iraqi measure.
He said, and he informed me that by weight it is one thousand one hundred and seventy weights.

key_terms.الصَّاع: A unit of volume measurement used for zakat and fitra
key_terms.الْعِرَاقِيِّ: Relating to Iraq, referring to the Iraqi standard of measurement
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra, the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.الْمَدَنِيِّ: Relating to Medina, referring to the Medinite standard of measurement

ai.seo_question: What is the weight of the Sa'a used for Fitra according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi resolves the juristic dispute regarding the measurement of the Sa'a for Fitra by distinguishing between the Medinite and Iraqi standards, reflecting the historical diversity in regional weights and measures. Imam al-Hadi (AS) provides precise conversions—six Ratls for the Medinite Sa'a and nine for the Iraqi—totaling 1,170 units, which serves as a foundational reference for Shia fiqh in calculating obligatory charity. This clarification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to specific, authenticated measurements to ensure the validity of religious obligations.
